v4.9.066 - the audit's work-eating list, done

#321 ./go: the terminal waits and asks; nothing long is pasted into a shell.
#322 Shooting orders, setups and groups were numbered per device from 1, so two
     people apart both made "sort_1" and the server saw one thing, not two. One
     person's order vanished; setups went further and mislabelled frames.
#323 On a pull the store was rebuilt from the old whole-project blob FIRST and
     the per-item settings merged on top, so the protection for unsent changes
     could only decline to overwrite what had already been overwritten. This is
     the vanishing break. What this device holds is now remembered before the
     rebuild and put back after it.
#324 ...and a settings change that survives a pull now says it still needs
     sending. A frame keeps its own record of being unsent; a shooting order has
     none, so the rescued break sat on one device for ever.
#325 A pull that died before touching anything was tidying up as though it had,
     recording every frame as safe in the cloud including unsent work. A drawing
     made just before the signal dropped was never uploaded and was overwritten.
#326 A frame's age now counts the newest thing done to it, the frame or any of
     its looks. It was judged on the frame alone while being CHOSEN on both, so
     a frame dirty only because of a new drawing had no time, lost by default,
     and its unsent look was rebuilt out of existence.
#327 A deletion survives closing the app, and no longer follows you into the
     next project where it was sent under the wrong project's name.

Two new tests (both devices making their first shooting order; a change made
while a pull is in the air), eleven in all, and a written audit of the sync
layer, the store, the schema and the migrations.
